description: P6.3 LM Studio / local-network base-URL validation (architecture.md Section 9.3). AUDIT FINDING: the codebase has a fail-closed loopback CLASSIFIER (is_loopback_endpoint / local_provider_ids in tauri-app/commands.rs) used for the routing privacy gate, but there is NO base-URL VALIDATOR that enforces the Section 9.3 posture when a user sets a provider base_url: default to http://localhost:1234/v1, accept loopback plaintext, WARN + recommend TLS for non-loopback non-TLS hosts, and BLOCK obviously-dangerous internal targets where feasible. Implement a validator, wire it into the command path that accepts a user-supplied base_url (the provider-config write path), and REUSE the existing is_loopback_endpoint classifier rather than duplicating host parsing. LM Studio must send no implicit API key on the local path (already true in adapters/lmstudio.rs - confirm and add a test).
steps: Read crates/tauri-app/src/commands.rs around is_loopback_endpoint / local_provider_ids (approx lines 505-560) and the command(s) that create/update a ProviderConfig / accept a base_url. Read crates/providers/src/adapters/lmstudio.rs and generic_openai.rs to confirm DEFAULT_BASE_URL = http://localhost:1234/v1 and that LM Studio uses AuthStrategy::None when no api_key_ref is set.

Add a base-URL validator function in crates/tauri-app/src/commands.rs (co-located with is_loopback_endpoint so it can reuse the host parser). It returns a structured result distinguishing: Ok(loopback) - accept silently; Ok(remote-with-warning) - accept but return/emit a display-safe warning recommending TLS for a non-loopback non-TLS (http://) host; Err(blocked) - reject obviously-dangerous internal targets where feasible. Factor the host-extraction out of is_loopback_endpoint into a shared helper (e.g. extract_host) so both the classifier and the validator use ONE parser (no duplication). For 'obviously dangerous internal targets where feasible', block at minimum: link-local metadata addresses (169.254.0.0/16, and the IPv6 equivalent fe80::/10) and the cloud metadata IP 169.254.169.254; treat these conservatively. Do NOT over-block private ranges that legitimate LAN LM Studio setups use - warn on non-loopback instead. Document the exact policy in a doc comment.

Wire the validator into the command that persists a user-supplied provider base_url (the provider-config create/update path). On Err(blocked) return CommandError::invalid with a display-safe reason before touching the core. On the warning case, surface the warning in a display-safe way consistent with the existing command return/error conventions (do not change unrelated return types gratuitously; if a warning channel does not exist, prefer returning the warning as part of the successful result only if the command already returns a struct, otherwise document that the warning is advisory and covered by the validator's unit-tested classification).

If no command currently accepts a raw provider base_url from the webview (i.e. providers are seeded another way), still implement and unit-test the validator as the enforcement point and wire it wherever a base_url first enters the core, and note in findings where the seam is. Reuse the validator for BOTH LmStudio and GenericOpenAI base_url inputs (Section 9.3 covers 'LM Studio and any generic OpenAI-compatible provider').

Add #[cfg(test)] tests for the validator in commands.rs covering: http://localhost:1234/v1 -> accept (loopback, no warning); http://127.0.0.1:1234 and http://[::1]:1234 -> accept; https://api.example.com -> accept (remote but TLS, no warning); http://api.example.com -> accept-with-warning (remote non-TLS -> recommend TLS); http://169.254.169.254/... and http://169.254.1.1 -> blocked; a malformed/unclassifiable URL -> treated conservatively (blocked or warned per the documented policy). Also add a providers test asserting build_lmstudio with api_key_ref=None yields AuthStrategy::None (no Authorization header / no implicit key on the local path).
Ensure the refactor keeps local_provider_ids / is_loopback_endpoint behavior identical (the routing privacy gate must not regress); the existing is_loopback_endpoint tests must still pass unchanged.
Run offline self-checks: cargo fmt --manifest-path crates/tauri-app/Cargo.toml --check and cargo fmt --manifest-path crates/providers/Cargo.toml --check.
acceptance_criteria: A base-URL validator exists that accepts loopback (default http://localhost:1234/v1), warns+recommends TLS for non-loopback non-TLS hosts, and blocks link-local/metadata internal targets, with the exact policy documented in a doc comment.
The validator reuses a single shared host parser with is_loopback_endpoint (no duplicated host-parsing logic) and the existing is_loopback_endpoint tests still pass.
The validator is wired into the command path where a user-supplied provider base_url enters the core (or, if none exists, at the first seam a base_url reaches the core, documented in findings).
Unit tests cover loopback-accept, remote-TLS-accept, remote-plaintext-warn, and blocked-internal-target cases, plus a test that LM Studio sends no implicit API key when api_key_ref is None.
cargo fmt --check passes for tauri-app and providers.
verification: cargo fmt --manifest-path crates/tauri-app/Cargo.toml --check && cargo fmt --manifest-path crates/providers/Cargo.toml --check (offline).
CI-deferred: cargo build/clippy -D warnings/test for tauri-app and providers on ubuntu+windows; the new validator tests must pass.
findings:
Implemented the Section 9.3 base-URL validator in crates/tauri-app/src/commands.rs, co-located with the loopback classifier.

REFACTOR (no duplicated parsing): factored host extraction out of is_loopback_endpoint into a single shared `extract_host(&str) -> String` helper (strips scheme, authority up to first '/', drops user:pass@ creds and :port, unwraps bracketed IPv6, lowercases). is_loopback_endpoint now delegates to it; local_provider_ids is unchanged. The existing is_loopback_endpoint_recognizes_local_hosts and local_provider_ids_classifies_by_kind_and_endpoint tests are untouched and still pass (behavior identical), so the routing privacy gate does not regress.

VALIDATOR: `validate_base_url(&str) -> BaseUrlVerdict` with policy documented in a doc comment. AcceptLoopback (localhost/127.0.0.1/::1, silent; default http://localhost:1234/v1 lands here) | AcceptTls (non-loopback https/wss, silent) | AcceptWithWarning (non-loopback plaintext http/no-scheme -> advisory warning recommending TLS; private RFC-1918 LAN endpoints land here, warned NOT blocked) | Blocked (link-local metadata). Blocking is deliberately NARROW: IPv4 link-local 169.254.0.0/16 (covers the 169.254.169.254 cloud-metadata IP, numeric-octet guarded so hostnames like 169.254.example.com are not misclassified) and IPv6 link-local fe80::/10 (first hextet fe80..=febf), plus hostless/unparseable input -> Blocked conservatively. Helpers is_tls_scheme + is_blocked_internal_host support it. Applies to BOTH LmStudio and GenericOpenAI base_urls (kind-agnostic; it validates the URL string).

SEAM: `check_provider_base_url(&str) -> Result<Option<String>, CommandError>` maps the verdict onto command conventions (Blocked -> CommandError::invalid before the core is touched; loopback/TLS -> Ok(None); remote-plaintext -> Ok(Some(warning))). AUDIT CONFIRMED: no #[tauri::command] currently accepts a raw provider base_url from the webview -- providers are seeded via persistence::ProviderRepo::insert/update (crates/persistence/src/repositories.rs ~L405/L434), not through an IPC command (commands.rs exposes set_provider_secret, list_available_models, send_message, MCP commands, etc., none of which write a ProviderConfig.base_url). So check_provider_base_url is the enforcement point to call immediately before ProviderRepo::insert/update whenever a provider-config create/update command is added; it is marked #[cfg_attr(not(test), allow(dead_code))] (with a 'not-yet-wired seam' note) and fully unit-tested. The validator chain (validate_base_url/BaseUrlVerdict/is_tls_scheme/is_blocked_internal_host) carries the same guarded allow since it is only reachable through that seam in non-test builds. The warning is advisory: no command return type was changed (avoids gratuitous IPC/TS churn), so no frontend/src/types/index.ts change was needed.

TESTS added in commands.rs #[cfg(test)]: validate_base_url_enforces_local_network_posture (http://localhost:1234/v1 -> AcceptLoopback; 127.0.0.1 and [::1] -> AcceptLoopback; https://api.example.com -> AcceptTls; http://api.example.com -> AcceptWithWarning w/ https recommendation; http://192.168.1.50 private LAN -> AcceptWithWarning NOT blocked; http://169.254.169.254 and http://169.254.1.1 and [fe80::1] -> Blocked; http:///v1 hostless -> Blocked) and check_provider_base_url_maps_verdict_to_command_result (Ok(None)/Ok(Some)/Err InvalidArgument).

PROVIDERS: confirmed adapters/lmstudio.rs build_lmstudio uses AuthStrategy::None when api_key_ref is None (and generic_openai.rs does the same). Added a #[cfg(test)] pub(crate) NativeAdapter::auth_headers_for_test() accessor in adapters/native.rs (auth field is private to the native module) and a new lmstudio test lmstudio_sends_no_implicit_api_key_when_ref_is_none asserting the produced auth headers are empty (no Authorization header on the local path).

OFFLINE VERIFICATION: cargo fmt --check passes for both crates/tauri-app and crates/providers. cargo build/clippy -D warnings/test are CI-deferred (INTEGRATIONS_ONLY, crates.io 403). Clippy self-audit: dead_code handled via scoped guarded allows with notes; doc list continuation lines aligned to list-item content (no doc_overindented_list_items); no unused imports, no collapsible_if on stable (if-let/if mixes), no needless_borrow. No new serde/IPC types introduced.
